mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate activity (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST declined for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period, it indicates strong consumer demand, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS growth exceeded CPIAUCSL growth over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS decreased by more than 100,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where the S&P 500 forward returns are positively correlated with the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the next 60 trading days, as lower rates typically stimulate economic activity and increase equity valuations.
failure_condition: If the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 60-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the growth rate of real GDP (GDPC1) exceeds the growth rate of the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over a 6-month period, it indicates strong economic demand without significant inflationary pressure, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 6 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 growth exceeded CPIAUCSL growth over a 6-month period.
